correctness.rationale: Exact source/target double integration gives F(g)/ell_1 and F(H-g)/ell_2. Bounded positive b_k guarantees finite F for arbitrary Borel probability measures; strict Holder equality yields complete non-Dirac log-convexity, the exact extremizers, and all boundaries. Diagonal similarity proves the many-reserve one-rate characteristic-polynomial law. Reproducible finite checks include multiple widths, multipliers and pure/mixed rates.

evidence: Hastings and Botsford (2006) give general graph-cycle persistence criteria for arbitrary matrices, but not the gap geometry of this positive-mixture family.
White et al. (2010) simulate retention zones and heterogeneous currents.
Blowes and Connolly (2012) analyze correlations and optimal spacing; abstract does not state exact Laplace-transform classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general Perron eigenvalue criterion alone does not imply monotone spacing or characterize the uniquely neutral rate law. The closest potentially broader optimal-spacing publication remains only abstract-accessible and is a nontrivial residual risk, explicitly disclosed.

evidence: The 2006 closed-loop theorem expresses general two-patch persistence in terms of return-loop products, but does not identify their strict log-convexity for positive mixtures.
The previously known one-rate point-site similarity is a limiting baseline; it does not imply a unique equal-gap minimum for non-Dirac mixtures.
Published advective-diffusive studies use different kernel families and objectives.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The logically new conclusion is: among all Borel exponential-rate mixtures, exactly Dirac measures make gap effects vanish; every other measure has a strict complete spacing order and threshold-crossing examples, including unequal interval lengths and site qualities. This is not implied by pure-rate invariance and is not an empirical/numerical result quoted in the read papers. A full-text unresolved 2012 comparison prevents certification of priority.
searches: Hyperexponential mixture of wrapped exponential larval dispersal: two-patch eigenvalue and strict optimal reserve placement, single-rate equality boundary

evidence: The two-reserve formula is exactly a product of the same Laplace transform at complementary gaps; single-rate point-site invariance is a known baseline.
Kaplan and Botsford (2005) use a two-sided Laplacian, and Kaplan (2006) uses an advective-shift Laplacian.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The conclusion is an all-positive-mixing-measures strict equality classification for finite intervals with fixed site quality. The earlier point-site pure-rate statement is strictly subsumed as baseline and is not independently claimed as a new theorem. A multirate law cannot be reduced by similarity to any one exponential because strict log-convexity forces nonconstant return-loop products.
searches: Sharp spacing optimization for two finite marine reserves under a mixture of clockwise exponential kernels: equal gaps uniquely minimize Perron root, touching gaps maximize, pure exponential yields spacing invariance
Completely monotone transport kernels are strictly log-convex so two-interval cyclic metapopulation connectivity is minimized by equal gaps for unequal patch lengths

evidence: The 2005 and 2010 studies show numerical spatial reserve configurations, not the continuum of all positive measures and widths.
The numeric illustrative threshold crossing follows from direct formulas, not from a table.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No identified published database, solved table, or finite numerical enumeration contains this all-parameter continuous optimization theorem. The absence of a discovered table is not itself treated as proof of novelty.

originality.rationale: Within inspected scientific evidence, the complete strict optimality for arbitrary exponential-rate mixtures in finite unequal reserves is not stated or implied by the point-site pure-rate baseline, Kaplan and Botsford 2005 simulations, Hastings and Botsford 2006 abstract matrix criteria, Kaplan 2006 shifted Laplacian, or White et al 2010 heterogeneous currents. Residual possibility of earlier equivalent completely monotone-kernel optimization is openly recorded; the 2012 paper is only abstract-accessible.
residual_risks: Full Blowes and Connolly (2012) text not accessible; cannot exclude hidden corollary of a broader reserve-spacing theorem.
An earlier general Laplace-transform/log-convexity result applied to two-patch reserve kernels might imply the statement without using identical terminology.
The one-rate point-site isospectral baseline is pre-existing and is not claimed as independently new.

value.rationale: A precise conservation-network design problem, studied empirically and numerically in primary ecological literature, has a complete analytic answer for all two-reserve lengths, site qualities, and positive exponential-rate mixtures. A natural distributional boundary (memoryless versus multiple transport scales) exactly separates placement neutrality from strict preference; an explicit unchanged-geometry threshold-crossing example demonstrates decision relevance. This is theoretical linear invasion analysis, not empirical advice.
